new_entities.name: N-acetylcysteine
new_entities.description: An acetylated cysteine derivative used as a glutamate-modulating and antioxidant adjunct in psychiatric trials.

new_entities.name: Obsessive-compulsive disorder severity
new_entities.description: Clinician-rated severity of obsessive-compulsive symptoms, usually measured with the Yale-Brown Obsessive Compulsive Scale.

edges.effect_quant: The most focused 2024 meta-analysis of NAC augmentation in OCD pooled six randomized trials and found a positive effect on total Y-BOCS scores only in the 5-to-8-week window, with no significant benefit at shorter or longer durations. A broader 2022 meta-analysis of mitochondrial modulators also found overall symptom improvement favoring NAC versus placebo, but not stronger response or remission outcomes.
edges.population: adults with moderate to severe obsessive-compulsive disorder receiving N-acetylcysteine as augmentation, usually on top of SSRI treatment
edges.mechanism: N-acetylcysteine may reduce obsessive-compulsive symptoms by modulating glutamatergic tone and redox balance within cortico-striatal circuits implicated in compulsivity. The signal remains inconsistent because the current literature is small, adjunctive, and heavily dependent on treatment duration and trial design.
edges.summary: N-acetylcysteine may modestly reduce OCD severity in some adults, but the evidence is still mixed rather than definitive. Meta-analytic signals are encouraging enough to justify research interest, yet they do not clearly establish durable benefit across longer treatment windows or stronger categorical outcomes.
edges.caveats: Most studies examine NAC as SSRI augmentation rather than monotherapy, and total samples remain small. This edge should be interpreted as a plausible adjunctive option with unresolved durability rather than as a proven OCD treatment.

evidence.notes: The safety and efficacy of N-acetylcysteine as an augmentation in the treatment of obsessive-compulsive disorder in adults: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials.
Mitochondrial modulators for obsessive-compulsive and related disorders: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
